summary: Source-anchored research for MongoDB 8.0 WT Improvements (TCMalloc, ExpressPlan). Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Percona's December 2025 test compares whole Percona Server versions 7.0.26-14 and 8.0.16-5 on Ubuntu 24.04 with four CPUs, 4 GB RAM and four workload threads. It reports gains that vary by operation. Because the versions contain multiple changes, these results do not isolate TCMalloc's contribution. (low confidence)

Treat TCMalloc and ExpressPlan as changes at different layers when analyzing WiredTiger performance: the former changes allocation and memory reuse, while the latter reduces query planning work before storage-engine access. Neither source establishes a replacement of WiredTiger’s on-disk structures. (medium confidence)

[redacted] reports that Express may perform shard filtering even when explain shows only EXPRESS_IXSCAN. Absence of a separate SHARDING_FILTER node in that output is therefore insufficient evidence that filtering was skipped. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-23)

TCMalloc per-CPU mode relies on Linux restartable sequences (rseq) to update CPU-local allocation structures without locking. MongoDB documents fallback to per-thread caches when glibc registers rseq first. (high confidence)

Check serverStatus.tcmalloc.usingPerCPUCaches and tcmalloc.tcmalloc.cpu_free to verify activation; MongoDB's tuning guide expects true and a positive byte count, respectively. MongoDB 8.0 also adds peak_memory_usage and per-CPU overflow/underflow metrics; serverStatus with tcmalloc:2 includes the cpuCache section. (high confidence)

To confirm per-CPU caching, inspect serverStatus.tcmalloc.usingPerCPUCaches for true and tcmalloc.tcmalloc.cpu_free for a positive value. MongoDB documents GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=0 before mongod starts and Linux kernel 4.18 or later when diagnosing disabled per-CPU caches. The kernel minimum alone does not establish compatibility with every newer kernel. (high confidence)

The documented upgraded-allocator platforms are supported Linux x86_64 and ARM64 systems. The same documentation says PPC64LE, s390x and Windows retain legacy TCMalloc, and instructs PPC64LE/s390x users to disable THP. (low confidence)

A May 2024 WiredTiger investigation, WT-13045, reported an approximately 5–6% medium-btree regression correlated with enabling new TCMalloc in performance tests. The workload built a 5 GB tree and used 16 random-read threads for two minutes. Increased resident memory reducing kernel page-cache capacity was a proposed explanation, not an established cause or proof of a regression in every released 8.0 build. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-05-26)

Percona traced a Docker allocator misconfiguration to getMemorySizeLimitInBytes in vendored cpu_cache.cc: atoll interpreted the cgroup value 'max' as zero. Its March 2026 account reports a fix shipped in Percona Server 8.0.16-5 and 36–60% higher throughput in four tested YCSB cases. These are fix-specific results, not general MongoDB 8.0 speedups. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-12)

Percona’s February 4, 2025 mongo-perf comparison of Percona Server for MongoDB 8.0.4 and 7.0.15 reported average improvements of 12%, 7% and 9% at one, four and eight threads respectively. It also reported some slower four-thread cases. These are results for that setup, not a universal speedup or an allocator-only measurement. (low confidence)

TechEmpower's March 2026 benchmark account distinguishes a TCMalloc Docker workaround from client connection-pool changes: its spring-mongo query result rose from 583 to 837 requests/s with the allocator workaround, and to 14.2k with both changes. The headline roughly 25x improvement therefore cannot be attributed to TCMalloc alone. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-16)

The cached MongoDB 8.0 release notes warn that the vendored TCMalloc is incompatible with Linux kernels 6.19 through 7.0.13 and recommend kernel 7.0.14 or later. They describe a startup guard against affected kernels. Recheck exact server patches, architecture and distribution backports before applying this warning operationally. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Per-CPU TCMalloc caches objects by logical CPU; its rseq fast path avoids locks. Per-thread caches can accumulate memory with thread count. This allocator mechanism concerns malloc/new and free/delete, rather than defining WiredTiger's page-cache policy. (medium confidence)

ExpressPlan addresses query-layer overhead: MongoDB's engineers traced simple _id lookups through general planning before IDHACK, then developed an Express path that bypasses regular planning for eligible queries. Treat it as a faster route to storage access, rather than a new WiredTiger on-disk format. (high confidence)

[redacted] records a possible tradeoff: choosing Express immediately for an eligible prefix can prevent an SBE-eligible $lookup pipeline from taking a faster path. The ticket proposes tests; it does not establish a MongoDB 8.0-wide slowdown or identify an affected release. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-27)

MongoDB 8.0 upgraded TCMalloc from per-thread to per-CPU caches on supported platforms, with the stated aims of reducing fragmentation and improving resilience under high-stress workloads. This is a server allocator change that also affects storage-engine allocations. (high confidence)

MongoDB 8.0 documents Express execution for a limited query set, including _id equality lookups. Explain stage names include EXPRESS_CLUSTERED_IXSCAN, EXPRESS_IXSCAN, EXPRESS_DELETE and EXPRESS_UPDATE; the feature does not imply that arbitrary queries skip planning. (high confidence)

For the upgraded allocator, MongoDB 8.0 documentation reverses the older THP recommendation: enable Transparent Huge Pages before mongod starts. This recommendation must be read together with allocator platform support; it is not a blanket instruction for every MongoDB platform or older release. (high confidence)

Per-CPU caches require rseq support. MongoDB documents Linux kernel 4.18 or later and disabling glibc rseq registration with GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=0; without usable rseq the allocator falls back to per-thread caches. A minimum kernel version is not a complete compatibility guarantee. (high confidence)

Per-CPU allocation caches avoid the thread-count scaling of legacy per-thread caches: Google documents a cache per logical CPU, with most cached allocations and deallocations avoiding locks. The middle-end still uses mutex-protected transfer caches and central free lists; the allocator is not universally lock-free. (high confidence)

ExpressPlan reduces the overhead before storage-engine access for eligible simple operations. MongoDB describes its origin in improving the _id IDHACK path and its expansion to updates, deletes and other unique-index lookups; the 8.0 explain documentation explicitly limits EXPRESS to a subset of queries that bypass regular planning. (high confidence)

End-to-end version benchmarks do not isolate the gain from TCMalloc or ExpressPlan. Percona compared Percona Server for MongoDB 8.0.16-5 and 7.0.26-14 with multiple workload mixes, while MongoDB describes numerous concurrent 8.0 optimizations; attributing the whole release gain to the allocator is unsupported by that experiment. (medium confidence)
